tiers.notes: The live card says 800 AI credits/maker/month, while an official FAQ describes 1,500 base credits plus 800 per additional maker; the conflict is retained rather than reconciled.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 50 AI credits/month/workspace; 500 feedback items; 25 contributors; 1 teamspace; 1 portal; minimum 1 maker.
pricing.billingTerms: Monthly + annual on self-serve plans; annual rates are roughly 21% lower; Enterprise is annual contract pricing.
pricing.hiddenCosts: AI top-ups cost $5/month for 50 credits on monthly billing or $60/year for 600 credits on annual billing; different AI tasks consume different credit quantities; credits reset monthly and mid-cycle upgrades are prorated.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Productboard, link manually imported feedback to features and a small roadmap. The hard boundary is customer-insight integrations, prioritization, roadmap governance, and organizational adoption, plus participant network, synthesis workflow, and collaboration.
coreLoopDIY: Collect manually imported feedback, merge duplicates, link evidence to features and a small roadmap, and publish a transparent status view.
whatYouLose: customer-insight integrations, prioritization, roadmap governance, and organizational adoption
moatNotes: participant network, synthesis workflow, and collaboration
ongoingBurden: recruitment, consent, scheduling, media storage, transcription, tagging consistency, notifications, search, and retention
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Productboard because people pay either for access to participants or for a research repository that keeps evidence usable across an organization. The recurring cost buys recruitment, consent, scheduling, media storage, transcription, tagging consistency, notifications, search, and retention, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Fider
priorArt.desc: Open-source customer-feedback portal with voting and status workflows.

alternatives.name: Quackback
alternatives.desc: Import feedback, merge the evidence, connect it to roadmap work and sync issues without buying a product suite.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Essentials plan and a small-team feedback repository DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Productboard in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Resend; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: collect manually imported feedback, merge duplicates, link evidence to features and a small roadmap, and publish a transparent status view.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create public and private feedback intake with consent text and optional contact details.
Support posts, votes, comments, tags, statuses, owners, and duplicate merging.
Add a research note type with evidence links, quotes, themes, and confidence.
Build search and filters across feedback, customers, segments, themes, and status.
Provide email notifications, moderation, export, deletion, and an audit log.
Publish a read-only roadmap or findings page using only explicitly public items.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out a paid research-participant marketplace.
Deliberately leave out unlimited video storage and automated transcription.
Deliberately leave out enterprise repositories, SSO, and governance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
